skill.name: gsap-utils
skill.description: Learn how to use GSAP utility methods in JavaScript animations. The reference covers numeric ranges, snapping, interpolation, per-target values, color parsing, and scoped element selection.
skill.summary: Use GSAP helpers to transform animation values and select targets.
skill.author: greensock

security_audit.summary: All 70 static findings are false positives: Markdown backticks mark code, URLs are GSAP references, and the reconnaissance matches describe colors or animation grids. The reviewed file contains no evidence of shell execution, unauthorized requests, system reconnaissance, or prompt injection.

content.user_title: Transform animation values with GSAP utilities
content.value_statement: Animation inputs often need to be converted, bounded, or snapped before they can drive a tween. This reference shows which GSAP helper to use and when to reuse it as a function.
actual_capabilities: Show how to bound numbers, map ranges, normalize inputs, and interpolate numbers, colors, or objects.
Show how to snap values to increments or allowed values and generate random values for tween targets.
Explain how to distribute tween values by target position in a list or grid.
Show how to extract CSS units and parse color strings into RGB or HSL components.
Demonstrate scoped selectors and conversion from selectors or DOM collections to arrays.
Combine reusable transforms with pipe and use wrap or wrapYoyo for repeating motion.
limitations: The skill is a reference and assumes GSAP is already available in the project.
The range helpers operate on numbers and do not convert between CSS units.
Selector examples require an available DOM and a valid container or ref.
The examples do not cover full timeline setup or component cleanup.

use_cases.title: Map scroll to rotation
use_cases.description: Turn scroll progress into an angle and clamp input that falls outside the expected range.

use_cases.title: Tune a stepped motion effect
use_cases.description: Use snap to keep an animated marker on a visual grid and compare different step sizes.

use_cases.title: Review component animation targets
use_cases.description: Check whether repeated components share a global selector and propose a selector scoped to each container.

prompt_templates.title: Clamp a progress value
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: bound progress before using it in an animation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Show how to clamp a numeric progress value between 0 and 1 with GSAP. Explain the results for -0.2, 0.5, and 1.2.

prompt_templates.title: Snap movement to a grid
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: reuse a helper for repeated position updates.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gsap.utils.snap to create a reusable helper that aligns horizontal positions to 20-pixel steps. Show what happens to 13, 38, and 62 pixels.

prompt_templates.title: Distribute scale within a component
prompt_templates.scenario: Applied: scope a tween to one grid of repeated elements.
prompt_templates.prompt: Scope the tween to my grid container and use gsap.utils.distribute to vary scale from the center to the edges. Explain how the base and amount affect the result.

prompt_templates.title: Compose a scroll transform
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: combine and test reusable transforms for a callback.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use gsap.utils.pipe to clamp scroll input to 0 through 800 pixels and map it to 0 through 360 degrees. Snap the result to 15-degree steps and list checks for below-range, midpoint, and above-range inputs.

output_examples.input: Clamp animation progress to 0 through 1. What happens to -0.2, 0.5, and 1.2?
output_examples.output: The first value becomes 0, the middle value stays at 0.5, and the last value becomes 1. Reuse the same clamping function for subsequent updates.

output_examples.input: Two components both contain elements named .item. How can I animate only the first component?
output_examples.output: Create a scoped selector from the first component container. Use its matching descendants as tween targets so the second component remains unchanged.

output_examples.input: Map scroll to rotation and snap it to 15-degree steps. What angle follows from 410 pixels in a range of 0 through 800?
output_examples.output: Mapping 410 pixels to a full rotation gives 184.5 degrees. The nearest 15-degree step is 180 degrees.

best_practices: Reuse a configured helper when the same bounds or snap increment applies to many updates.
Scope selectors to a component container before selecting its animation targets.
Test endpoints and out-of-range inputs when combining mapping, clamping, and snapping.
anti_patterns: Pass CSS strings directly to numeric range helpers.
Use a document-wide selector for class names shared by independent components.
Assume mapRange or normalize clamps values outside the input range.

faq.question: Do GSAP utility methods need plugin registration?
faq.answer: No. The methods are available on gsap.utils whenever GSAP core is loaded.

faq.question: How do I create a reusable range helper?
faq.answer: For clamp, mapRange, and normalize, omit the input value to get a function. Call that function with each new value.

faq.question: How do I get a reusable random generator?
faq.answer: Pass true as the final argument to gsap.utils.random. The returned function produces a new sample each time you call it.

faq.question: What is the difference between mapRange and clamp?
faq.answer: Use mapRange to convert a value from one scale to another. Use clamp to enforce minimum and maximum bounds.

faq.question: When should I use selector instead of toArray?
faq.answer: Use selector to create a reusable query for one container. Use toArray when you need an array from a selector, collection, or single element.

faq.question: How do wrap and wrapYoyo differ?
faq.answer: Use wrap to cycle through a range. Use wrapYoyo to reverse direction at the range boundaries.
